cases.title: New learner opening on a busy comp

rubric.reason: The opening reports the scan ("11 keyframe pairs that need easing, across 6 layers") and proposes a starting layer without being asked: "I suggest we start with **Title**."
It proposes one layer (Title) and names five pairs in total, Title's 4 plus Subtitle's Opacity, which is within the 5-pair limit; every other layer appears only as a count.

It names hidden_layers Old Take ("you've hidden it, so I'll skip it") and precomp Icon ("I can't see inside those yet, so I'm not saying it's fine"), each with a reason, and doesn't imply the precomp is fine.

Every name and time matches snapshot_project: 11 = 10 linear + 1 partly_eased; 6 layers are Title, Subtitle, CTRL, Bar, Glow and Old Take; Subtitle Opacity's linear_end "end" matches "eased at the start but still linear at the end"; Title's Position 0.5–1.5 s and 1.5–3 s, Scale and Opacity 0.5–1.5 s all match.

read_learner_record ran before snapshot_project and returned an empty record (no skills, no lessons); the mentor claims no history ("Welcome to your first easing lesson") and doesn't mention the file or its fields.

The opening carries the count, the Title proposal and the leave-outs as one choice, explains nothing about easing, and ends on a single question about the layer ("Shall we start with Title, or would you like to pick a different layer?").
